analysis.title: 2027 Global Strategy Outlook: Embracing Risk
key_insights: Morgan Stanley moves to maximum overweight global equities for 2027, adding to every region and lifting Japan and Europe to OW. It funds this from fixed income, commodities and cash. The case rests on an intact AI capex cycle, resilient macro and cheaper valuations.

Equities: S&P 500 4Q27 target is 8,700 (19x forward EPS of $458), MSCI Europe 3,030, TOPIX 4,800 and MSCI EM 1,760. EM stays equal-weight because China faces deflation and low nominal growth. Bear cases are -20% or worse in every index, so the bull-bear ranges are unusually wide.

Global ACWI EPS growth is forecast to slow from +37% in 2026E to +13% in 2027E and +8% in 2028E. MS estimates are 9% below bottom-up consensus by end-2028. ACWI forward P/E has fallen to about 15x, the lowest since 2023 and about 5 points below a year ago, as real rates rose. MS expects this valuation headwind to fade.

AI capex: MS projects hyperscaler cash capex including leases of $1,703bn in 2027E and $1,815bn in 2028E. Global data center capacity additions are 40 GW in 2027E and 43 GW in 2028E. The US midterm results shift about 5 GW of US projects from 2028 to 2029 but leave aggregate capex unchanged. Data center restrictions are seen as a state-level story, with no federal pause expected.

Capex mix shifts toward IT hardware in 2027, about 65% of the cost of bringing capacity online. Memory prices and newer chips raise unit costs. About $800bn of the $1.2tn IT hardware spend is by high-quality hyperscalers and about $420bn by lower-rated hyperscalers, neoclouds and others. 2027 is expected to be the year chip financing dominates the AI financing debate.

Debt financing of AI: MS expects $940bn of aggregate AI-related issuance in 2027, up from about $650bn in 2026. This includes $410bn of global unsecured hyperscaler issuance (+25%), $350bn of structured chip financing, $60bn of secured data center project bonds (-25%) and $35bn of data center ABS and CMBS. Debt rises less than capex because equity raises, cash flow and lower shareholder returns also fund it.

Asset allocation: OW equities (+15% vs benchmark), EW core fixed income (-4%), UW other fixed income (-5%) and UW commodities (-3%). US IG moves to EW from UW, HY is cut to UW, EM local goes to UW, and Brent and copper go to UW. USTs stay neutral as a portfolio hedge, and MS argues the stock-bond correlation concern is overdone.

Quality bias: MS pairs risk-taking with quality because tails are long. It favors strong balance sheets and durable margins in US equities, IG over sub-IG in credit, loans over HY bonds, and the top of the capital structure such as CLO AAAs. Weaker, levered borrowers are more exposed to higher rates.

Macro baseline: global growth about 3.4% in 2027, US growth 2.5% (4Q/4Q), and two more hikes each from the Fed, ECB and BoJ over the next 12 months. MS sees the Fed at a 4.375% midpoint by March 2027, the ECB deposit rate at 3.00% and the BoE at 4.50%. Cuts in the US, euro area and UK start in 2028. MS calls these recalibrations and not a cycle that stalls GDP or earnings.

Rates: 4Q27 targets are UST 10Y 5.00%, DBR 10Y 3.10%, UKT 10Y 5.00% and JGB 10Y 2.95%. MS expects yields below forwards across most of G10, with the most value in Bunds and gilts. Treasuries bear flatten in 1H27 and steepen in 2H27. Gilts are about 45bp below forwards. The JGB 10s30s steepener is maintained as a top trade.

FX: DXY is forecast to 105, EUR/USD 1.08, USD/JPY 162, GBP/USD 1.27 and AUD/USD 0.72 by 4Q27. The Carry Regime continues, with wider USD-rest-of-world rate differentials. EUR is a funder as French presidential election risk builds in spring 2027. GBP is a key underperformer, and AUD, NZD and SEK outperform.

Credit: US IG spreads are forecast to tighten to 80bp, US HY to 310bp and loans to 430bp. MS expects US IG issuance of $2.4tn (+12%) and defaults rising to 4.5% in HY and 4.75% in loans. It closes its high-conviction IG underweight, takes off its underweight on high-quality hyperscalers, and stays neutral on data center debt. It likes CDX decompression, long IG equity tranches vs index and buying French bank CDS vs senior financials.

Securitized: favorites are CLO AAAs and non-QM across the stack. Agency MBS is neutral and agency CMBS is preferred. Regulatory tailwinds such as Basel Endgame changes and lower supply support demand. Data center AAA ABS at about +200bp needs structural deleveraging to draw more demand.

Commodities: gold is the top pick at $5,250/oz by 4Q27 ($5,000 by 2Q27). Brent is forecast to normalize to $75/bbl by 4Q27, with $100 kept for 1Q27. MS sees a 1.4 mb/d crude surplus in 4Q26. Copper is forecast at $12,800/t and is tight near term, with US tariff policy the main 2027 uncertainty. Gold held up well relative to real yields because of central bank and ETF demand.

EM fixed income: valuations are rich versus USTs and rate differentials are compressed, so MS favors alpha over beta. It forecasts EMBIG Div at 200bp by 4Q27, prefers BB over EM IG, likes HUF, MYR, SGD, KRW and PEN, and is cautious on THB, IDR, PHP, COP and PLN. An Iran deal with lower oil is the EM bull case.

Europe equities: MSCI Europe target of 3,030 assumes the forward P/E rises to 16x from 14.4x as the discount to the US narrows. Earnings growth slows in 2027 on a smaller Energy contribution. Europe is skewed to 'pure' AI adopters (over 60% of index weight vs 30% for the S&P) and is exposed to any Strait of Hormuz reopening. A wave of 2027 elections, including France, is a risk.

Risks: stronger-than-expected AI capex would lift earnings but could pressure credit spreads. An abrupt end to the AI cycle would hit equities and credit and spark a safe-haven bid for governments. Brent retesting $115/bbl would reprice the Fed and ECB paths and push yields above forecasts. Reacceleration of inflation with more tightening is another risk.

Quant: MS likes equity factors, volatility carry (outright over relative value) and FX carry. For the US it favors EPS up-vs-down revisions, low PEG and R&D-to-market cap. Cross-asset realized skewness is expected to benefit from reversals of 2026 moves.

sector_views.rationale: OW Industrials, Financials and Discretionary. UW Staples, Real Estate and Energy. Style preference is quality cyclicals, AI adopters and hyperscalers within the AI compute trade.
OW Banks, Semis, Metals and Mining, Capital Goods and Aerospace. UW Luxury, Software, Autos, Medtech and P&P.
OW Non-Bank Financials, Construction and Materials, Raw Materials and Chemicals, Machinery and IT Services. UW Energy, Foods, Pharma, Trading Companies and Transport.
EW overall. OW Industrials, Semis and IT, Materials and Energy. UW Consumer Discretionary, Consumer Staples and Telcos. Korea preferred to Taiwan on valuations.
Utilities benefit from AI-driven power demand and BDCs have kept primary market access through software disruption fears.
EW core fixed income. Favor Bunds and gilts duration, keep USTs near forwards as a hedge to max OW equities.
Brent and copper cut to UW on negative forecast returns, while gold stays the top commodity pick outright.

earnings_insights: MS top-down ACWI EPS growth forecast is +13% for 2027E and +8% for 2028E after +37% in 2026E. These are bank forecasts, not reported results.
S&P 500 EPS forecast: $369 in 2026E (34% growth), $420 in 2027E (14% growth) and $458 in 2028E (9% growth). These are MS estimates.
TOPIX EPS growth forecast of +13% for calendar 2027 is in line with consensus. EM EPS growth forecast of +17% is below consensus at +29%, mainly on a cautious MSCI China view.
MSCI Europe 2026E EPS growth is nearly 22%, with 760bp from Energy. Ex-Energy growth is 15%. Earnings are expected to decelerate in 2027 on lower Energy contribution.

In the US, 44% of S&P 500 companies cite at least one quantifiable benefit from AI adoption, up from 32% a year ago, per MS equity research surveys. The median Russell 3000 stock is delivering mid-teens EPS growth.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Growth holds steady and supports earnings and AI-related demand.
AI spending and high-income consumers underpin demand.
Core inflation eases from 3.2% in 2026E but stays above the Fed's 2% target.
Two more hikes, then a hold, with cuts beginning in 1H28 to 3.625% by end-2028.
Two further 25bp hikes in December 2026 and March 2027, then a hold, with cuts toward 2.25% by end-2028.
Two more 25bp hikes versus about 4.9% market-implied peak, which supports gilts.
Hikes continue, with the 10-year JGB sector expected to outperform both wings.
Yields rise in 1H27, with 10Y at 5.05% mid-year, before the front end rallies in 2H27.
Gives markets a better read of Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's reaction function, with less forward guidance expected.
Normalization from about $100 in 1Q27 as supply recovers and risk premium fades.

trade_ideas.description: Maximum overweight global equities, funded from fixed income, commodities and cash
trade_ideas.rationale: Intact AI capex cycle, strong trend earnings growth and de-rated valuations.
trade_ideas.risk: Reacceleration of inflation with more tightening, or an abrupt end to the AI capex cycle.

trade_ideas.description: Long duration in Bunds and gilts
trade_ideas.rationale: Markets price more BoE hikes than MS expects and less ECB easing in 2028.
trade_ideas.risk: Aggregate demand upside scenario, which is most bearish for gilts.

trade_ideas.rationale: Weak growth can weigh on long-term risk premium, and fiscal expansion can weigh on the long end.
trade_ideas.risk: BoJ appearing further behind the curve as firms pass through higher costs.

trade_ideas.description: Long CDX IG 0-3% equity tranche vs index (CDX IG 0-3% at 891bp, CDX IG at 59bp)
trade_ideas.rationale: Takes advantage of the cheapening in AI-related spreads.
trade_ideas.risk: Further deterioration in AI sentiment causing another leg wider in spreads.

trade_ideas.description: CDX index decompression, HY vs IG (CDX IG 59bp, CDX HY 348bp)
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher rates reinforce the safe-haven status of US IG while sub-IG credit metrics are more vulnerable.
trade_ideas.risk: A rally in rates could lead CDX HY to outperform IG.

trade_ideas.description: Buy French bank CDS vs sell iTraxx Senior Financials
trade_ideas.rationale: French bank CDS screens rich relative to sovereign CDS and is a cheap hedge into an election-heavy year.
trade_ideas.risk: If fiscal and election uncertainty fades, French banks could outperform senior financials.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer US leveraged loans over HY bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: Better total returns in a policy tightening cycle.
trade_ideas.risk: Elevated software exposure drives higher loan defaults.

trade_ideas.description: Short EUR vs high-carry EM currencies, carry funded in EUR or JPY
trade_ideas.rationale: EUR is the funder of choice as election risk premium builds, and some of MS's strongest FX return projections are short EUR vs high-carry EM.
trade_ideas.risk: A broad risk-off move or stronger US demand lifting the USD.

trade_ideas.description: Long gold, the top commodity pick, target $5,250/oz by 4Q27
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong physical demand from central banks and ETFs, with Middle East de-escalation lowering oil and rate expectations as the clearest route higher.
trade_ideas.risk: Rising rate hike expectations and a stronger USD.

trade_ideas.description: Long Hungarian duration and HUF in EM
trade_ideas.rationale: Euro adoption gains credibility, supported by fiscal consolidation and risk-premium compression.

risk_factors: Abrupt end to the AI investment cycle, which would pressure equities, credit and positioning concentrated in tech.
Brent retesting $115/bbl, repricing Fed and ECB paths and pushing yields above MS forecasts.
Inflation reacceleration forcing tightening beyond the two further US hikes in the baseline.
Heavy AI-related credit issuance pressuring spreads, which is macro insensitive.
Tariff decisions, including copper tariffs and the USMCA review.
French and other European elections in 2027 and fiscal slippage in France.
US data center restrictions at the state level, plus labor, on-site generation and emissions constraints.
Higher funding costs for levered and lower-rated borrowers, and refinancing risk.
charts_described: Exhibit 6 lists 2027e hyperscaler cash capex including leases at 1,703 and 2028e at 1,815 ($bn), global data center capacity addition of 40 GW and 43 GW, and 2027 unsecured hyperscaler issuance of $410bn.
Exhibit 24 shows est. total cost of capacity added of $1,880bn in 2027E and AI capex at 91% of that, with IT hardware at 65% of cost.
Exhibit 7 states the bull-bear range for MSCI EM forecasts is the widest in the last 5 years.
Exhibit 28 states ACWI forward P/E has fallen to only 15x versus a peak of over 20x as real rates rose.
Exhibit 59 states credit index ranges were the narrowest in over two decades.
vol_and_positioning: MS likes volatility carry strategies, especially outright selling of volatility, for investors who can tolerate intermittent drawdowns. Past sell-offs in vol carry were good entry points over the last two years.
Among relative value volatility strategies, MS prefers VIX-space strategies.
Cross-asset realized skewness is expected to benefit from distress and reversals, given MS expects some 2026 moves to reverse in 2027.
FX volatility has been muted because interest rate differentials moved little despite large moves in rate levels, which amplified carry demand.
Credit indices traded in their narrowest range in over two decades, while CCC spreads widened to over 1000bp.
Tech concentration in indices and in positioning would amplify losses if AI capex slowed sharply.
geopolitical: The Middle East conflict and the Strait of Hormuz (SoH) disruption keep driving energy volatility. A US-Iran deal and full SoH reopening is the bull case for lower oil and EM assets.
The Ukraine conflict continues to affect the energy complex.
Europe faces elections in 2027, including the French presidential election in spring, plus Italy, Greece and German state elections.
US tariff risk remains, with the USMCA review and Sec. 232 actions as key catalysts. MS sees scope for marginally higher tariffs after the midterms.

US-China: base case is an extension of managed competition. Three Busan consensus components expire in early January, including the 178 Section 301 exclusions, the BIS Affiliates Rule suspension and China's second-wave rare-earth controls.
US midterms gave Democrats control of both House and Senate and governorships in Texas and Ohio. MS expects little change in executive-driven policy volatility.
cross_bank_references: MS bullish gold forecast is above Bloomberg consensus, and MS is more bearish than consensus on EUR, GBP and JPY.
MS ECB view is 'Well against consensus' on cutting toward neutral in 2028.
MS ACWI EPS estimates are 9% below bottom-up consensus by end-2028.

tension_points.bull_case: MS sees hyperscaler capex of about $1.7trn in 2027 and $1.8trn in 2028, with adoption ROI visible as 44% of S&P 500 companies cite quantifiable AI benefits. Stronger capex could lift AI ROIC and drive equities above the base case.
tension_points.bear_case: A significant slowdown in AI capex would pressure equities given tech concentration in indices and positioning, and credit would sell off in sympathy. Capex FCF turns more negative and funding needs rise.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A very significant slowdown in hyperscaler and AI-related capex below MS's $1.7trn 2027 projection, or yields taking another leg up on funding concerns for AI projects.

tension_points.bull_case: Brent normalizes to $75/bbl, headline and core inflation fall, central banks finish hiking by early 2027 and the ACWI P/E rerates from 15x as the valuation headwind fades.
tension_points.bear_case: Reacceleration of inflation forces tightening beyond the two further US hikes, with the aggregate demand upside scenario taking the Fed to 5.375% and 10Y yields to 5.90%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Brent retesting $115/bbl and above, or consumer spending strengthening with unemployment falling, which would push yields toward the bear case.

tension_points.theme: US HY and levered credit vs high-quality credit
tension_points.bull_case: IG gets better risk-reward on repricing and anchored capex expectations, and US IG excess returns are forecast among the highest in 5 years.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher rates hurt levered and lower-rated borrowers, with HY and loan defaults rising to 4.5% and 4.75% and chip financing competing for capital.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rally in rates, which could let CDX HY outperform IG and undermine the decompression trade.

theme_stances.key_argument: Baseline AI capex projections are intact despite midterm policy uncertainty, with only a timing shift from 2028 to 2029.
theme_stances.evidence: Morgan Stanley Research has high conviction in our view that the AI capex cycle remains intact

theme_stances.evidence: We move to maximum OW in global equities

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher rates raise uncertainty for levered and lower-rated borrowers, so prefer IG over sub-IG and loans over HY bonds.
theme_stances.evidence: Across regions, we prefer IG to sub-IG.
